correctness.rationale: For every fixed normal, upper and lower supporting offsets contribute t²/(8rho) each; compactness and positive curvature give uniform asymptotics, so g=w/P and b=(rho^{-1}+rho_pi^{-1})/(8P). With known P, w+w''=rho+rho_pi and 8Pb=rho^{-1}+rho_pi^{-1}; their sum/product yields the unordered radii from a quadratic. Equality of analytic antipodal differences squared forces one global sign by the real-analytic identity principle, so the support functions differ only by a translation or a point reflection. For the smooth counterfamily, each phi_j=psi_j''+psi_j has zero first Fourier harmonic, so its pi-antiperiodic extension yields valid positive radii; constant width follows from antipodal sum, and disjoint supports ensure equal squares (hence equal inverse-curvature sums). Exact ellipse checks, Fourier quadratures, analytic-pairing tests and smooth squared-identity tests were run from the included code. None of these numerical checks replaces the proof.

originality.rationale: Primary inspected papers prove full or neighborhood covariogram reconstruction and in one case unordered antipodal curvature extraction, but retain strictly more input than the pair of directional functions used here. The present implication is a new truncated-data theorem with an analyticity-versus-C-infinity separation; full covariogram uniqueness does not imply such limited-data uniqueness. published-finding corpus queries for short-chord, width, antipodal curvature, and analyticity returned no matching or dominating claim, including related constant-width and inverse width entries. Risk remains for older integral-geometry chapters not read in full and for alternate terminology.

value.rationale: The two-function reduction is a meaningful inverse-geometric compression of the full directional chord data used in covariogram tomography. The construction proves a genuine smooth-class boundary even among positively curved constant-width bodies, not a normalization artifact. It distinguishes exactly which data resolve antipodal curvature ambiguity under analyticity and supplies explicit natural smooth nonuniqueness. This is a motivated structural result and not a finite table or a minor numerical refinement.
